Hi Alex —

Thanks again for your time on the demo earlier today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can scope procurement for the pilot: 

- Goal: 3-week pilot (hosted Redwood API) with telemetry-only data retention, capped spend $6k.
- Commercial path: your PM mentioned AP prefers POs for vendor onboarding but engineering is OK with card for smaller pilots. Can you confirm which is required for purchase order creation?
- Marketplace: Is procurement open to AWS Marketplace procurement (would make invoicing simpler) or does OrionBio require vendor onboarding directly?

Attached is a draft SOW and a short purchase checklist that procurement asked for. If AP requires a formal PO, can you put me in touch with the person who owns vendor setup (name/email would be great)?

Next steps I propose:
1) If PO is required, we'll share SOW + W-9 + sample invoice to speed vendor setup.
2) If card is acceptable for the pilot, we can issue a card invoice and start within 48 hours after payment.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call with your AP to unblock this.

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side:

- AP policy: OrionBio prefers POs for any vendor spend that requires vendor creation in our ERP. That said, for trial/pilot spend under $5,000 we can accept a virtual credit card (one-off) to accelerate onboarding.
- Marketplace: Procurement generally prefers direct vendor onboarding for our regulated buyers; AWS Marketplace purchases complicate internal chargeback for projects tied to clinical research. So prefer direct vendor.
- Vendor contact: looping in Finance AP (ap@orionbio.com) and Sam Patel (CTO). Sam — AP will share vendor setup steps.

I can confirm pilot budget is $6k but we have some flexibility: if we split initial purchase (card) and follow with a PO for the remainder, would that be acceptable?

Onward —
Alex
Head of Product
OrionBio

Kim / Lauren —

Thanks for the thread. A few notes from GTM & pricing perspective as we decide whether to recommend card-first or PO-first: 

- If we accept a split (card for first $4k, PO for remainder), operationally we'll need to issue two invoices and ensure billing is tied to same account/HubSpot deal. That's fine but requires manual reconciliation on both sides.
- If OrionBio requires direct vendor onboarding (per Alex), that adds ~7 business days on average for net-30 PO approval — could push pilot start beyond the ideal window.
- Marketplace route: if they accept a marketplace contract, billing flows and tax are handled externally but we lose some visibility for invoice-level usage telemetry; it's simpler for procurement.

Suggested path: propose virtual card to start (expedites timeline) while simultaneously starting vendor onboarding for a PO. That hedges risk and keeps the pilot timeline intact.

I'll draft a short note for AP that summarizes what we need (W-9, remit address, tax form, sample invoice) and attach procurement-options.pdf to share.

Rishi
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the thread and the attachments. A quick summary of OrionBio's vendor onboarding and AP rules: 

1) Standard onboarding: vendor creation requires a completed vendor form, a W-9 (for US entities), remit address, and a sample invoice. Typical turnaround for new vendors is 7–10 business days.
2) PO policy: We operate on net-30 terms for PO-based invoices. Any spend that requires a vendor record must flow via PO once vendor is created.
3) Virtual card exception: For pilot projects under $7,500 we can approve a one-time virtual card to expedite procurement. This is an exception and requires sign-off from the CTO (Sam).

Action items for Redwood to expedite: 
- Please complete and return the vendor questionnaire here: https://orionbio.sharepoint.com/form/vendor-setup
- Provide W-9 and remit address (can send as PDF).
- If you prefer the virtual card route, please confirm the card holder name and invoice line item description we should expect.

If you send the vendor packet today we can start onboarding and potentially approve the virtual card before the end of the week (subject to Sam's sign-off).

Regards,
AP Team
OrionBio
